newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Foster Wheeler in Venezuelan oil technology deal.
newsitem.headline: Foster Wheeler in Venezuelan oil technology deal.

text.p: U.S. engineers Foster Wheeler and UOP signed a technology alliance with Venezuela's state oil technology company Intevep to market a new extra-heavy crude processing called Aquaconversion, Intevep said in a statement on Thursday.
The process is a type of catalytic conversion with similar effects as visbreaking, used to ease the transport and refining of extra-heavy crude, the statement said.

It is a patent of Intevep, itself a subsidiary of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA), and was tested in PDVSA's Curacao refinery. Aquaconversion can also be used before delayed coking to cut the residual fuel oil and raise vacuum gas oil yield of crude oil.
Intevep said the technology could be applied to 129 refineries around the world and was negotiating a deal to install the system in a thermal cracker at the Curacao refinery.

Intevep is already in the design stages of an aquaconversion plant in the Cerro Negro area of Venezuela's Orinoco extra-heavy crude oil belt, where production is expected to reach 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) by 2000-2001.
The technology can be used to double the API of heavy crude oil, removing the need for diluents, Intevep said.
